claims.claim: L5 Caco-2 bidirectional transport for the coumarins decursin and decursinol shows high apparent permeability (11.1 and 18.3 ×10^-6 cm/s) with efflux ratios of 1.0-1.1, indicating passive diffusion without a significant gut-wall efflux barrier.

Calycosin, a methoxy/phenolic isoflavone, has a Caco-2 Papp of about 3.5 ×10^-5 cm/s and an efflux ratio below 1.5, and crosses membranes by passive diffusion, supporting favorable intestinal absorption for small methoxy/phenolic aromatics.

Genkwanin, a 7-methoxy flavone, shows high rat intestinal effective permeability (P_eff 1.97 ×10^-4 cm/s) in single-pass intestinal perfusion, indicating efficient absorptive transport for a methoxy/phenolic aromatic compound.

Methylated flavones 7,4'-DMF, 5,7-DMF, and 7-MF show high Caco-2 Papp values (25.0, 23.3, and 22.6 ×10^-6 cm/s), and methylated flavones are considerably more permeable than their unmethylated analogues, supporting the favorable absorption of the query's methoxy-substituted coumarin scaffold.
Formononetin, a methoxy isoflavone, has a Caco-2 A→B Papp of 16.1 ×10^-6 cm/s and an efflux ratio of 1.0-1.5, indicating no significant active efflux.

Baicalein and wogonin are easily absorbed across Caco-2 monolayers with high permeability and low glucuronide formation in the gut-wall model, providing no evidence of an intrinsic efflux or intestinal-metabolism barrier for small phenolic aglycones.

L3 oral Cmax records for small phenolics (paeonol 8.61 µg/mL at 70 mg/kg in rats; BHA about 2 µg/mL in mice) and L4 Caco-2 classifications of decursin and decursinol angelate as well absorbed, plus good oral absorption of paeonol and veratric acid, support measurable oral absorption for the query's small phenolic/coumarin scaffold.

The low-F records for chrysin and acacetin concern larger polyphenolic flavones with very low solubility and extensive conjugation; they are not transferable to the small, moderately lipophilic coumarin scopoletin and do not provide affirmative threshold-relevant evidence for F < 20%.
